title: Keeper: Conductor for taskified admin utilities and runbook microactions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce 'Keeper', a lightweight conductor that converts existing runbooks and admin scripts into versioned, idempotent tasklets that can be scheduled, simulated, and executed with RBAC and dry-run safety gates. Keeper is intended to reduce oncall cognitive load, increase repeatability of fixes, and enable observability + rollback for human-invoked remediation. This ticket covers the MVP: tasklet packaging, an execution agent shim, RBAC checks, dry-run/preview mode, and telemetry hooks for run success, latency, and authorization events.
acceptance_criteria: Package: Existing runbook snippets can be packaged into a tasklet manifest (yaml) with name, inputs, estimated cost, and run constraints
Executor: A containerized exec shim can run a tasklet in sandbox mode and production mode with identical inputs
RBAC: Tasklet execution requires a signed authorization token and is rejected if the caller lacks role permissions (integrates with SSO groups)
Dry-run: Dry-run mode executes planning steps and validation checks without making state changes; dry-run output recorded in console logs and UI
Telemetry: Each execution emits telemetry events (tasklet.start, tasklet.complete, tasklet.error, tasklet.preview) to the ops metrics pipeline
Safety: Tasklets executed with a configurable safety timeout and automatic rollback hooks when a step fails
Docs: Confluence PR created describing packaging format, CLI commands, and runbook migration steps
technical_notes: Tasklet manifest schema v0.1: name, version, inputs, outputs, steps (shell/container), required_roles, timeout_seconds, idempotency_key_spec
Executor will be a small Go binary (keeper-agent) that runs as a privileged sidecar on Dedicated clusters and as an ephemeral job in Hosted for self-serve flows
Idempotency will rely on explicit idempotency_key_spec + centralized idempotency store (redis-backed with ttl) to prevent double-execution during retries
Dry-run implemented via 'plan' hooks in steps; each step may declare a non-mutating preview command where possible
RBAC integration: use existing SSO/SAML groups via platform-authz; signed execution token issued by Console service with aud:keeper and exp
Safety net: orchestrator monitors step heartbeats and triggers compensating steps declared in manifest on failure
Observability: instrument with trace-id propagation, attach request_id to logs; emit metrics to telemetry.ingest (redwood.ops.tasklet.*)
Compatibility: design manifests so we can later transpile existing runbook fragments from the Runbook DSL to Keeper tasklets
migration_plan: Inventory: runbook-catalog export to identify top 50 high-frequency remediation scripts (billing, node-restart, cache-clear)
Pilot: convert 5 highest-priority runbooks into tasklets (low-risk ones first) and test in staging with the keeper-agent
Training: run a 2-hour ops workshop to walk support engineers through packaging + dry-run flows
Rollout: enable Keeper for a subset of firstline support team in beta, capture feedback and iterate
Backfill: create automated lint script to detect non-idempotent patterns in runbook snippets and flag for refactor
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and idempotency key generation
Integration test: keeper-agent executes packaged tasklet in ephemeral k8s job and reports telemetry events
Fuzz test: feed malformed manifests to ensure graceful validation errors
Chaos test: simulate step failure and verify compensating steps and telemetry capture
E2E staging run with live SSO tokens and dry-run toggled to verify authz gating
rollout_plan: Week 1: deploy keeper-agent to staging and run pilot tasklets with ops engineers
Week 2: extend to Dedicated test cluster; enable RBAC enforcement; collect telemetry
Week 3: soft launch to 20% of firstline; monitor errors and MTTR metrics closely
Week 4: full internal rollout and Confluence + CLI docs published; schedule postmortem review after 2 weeks
metrics: Time to remediate (MTTR) for pilot runbooks: target -20% within 30 days
Tasklet success rate >= 98% after pilot stabilization
Reduction in manual runbook variance: all pilot runs must be executed via Keeper in 30 days
Number of dry-runs performed (adoption indicator): target 100 dry-runs in first month
Authorization failures (operational): < 0.5% of attempts should be RBAC-related after mapping
risks: Non-idempotent scripts may cause state corruption if converted naively; mitigated by lint and manual review
Authz mismatch with external SSO groups could block legitimate runs; mitigation: allow emergency bypass with audit trail
Telemetry overload: a surge in preview dry-runs could spike metrics; mitigation: sampling and rate limits
Executor bug causing unexpected side effects; mitigation: sandboxed staging harness and automatic rollbacks
